source.title: Seasonal and elevational variations of black carbon and dust in snow and ice in the Solu-Khumbu, Nepal and estimated radiative forcings

bc_albedo_reduction_pct.note: Relative to clean snow; from instantaneous radiative forcing model at Mera Glacier elevations

bc_forcing_W_m2.note: Instantaneous, localized radiative forcing from BC alone

dust_albedo_reduction_pct.note: Relative to clean snow; substantially larger than BC contribution

dust_forcing_W_m2.note: Instantaneous, localized radiative forcing from dust; dominates over BC at this site

combined_bc_plus_dust_additional_bc_forc.note: Additional forcing from BC when combined with dust; BC contribution becomes negligible relative to dust when dust concentrations are elevated

dust_to_bc_forcing_ratio.note: Dust forcing is approximately 4–7× larger than BC forcing at Mera Glacier

key_finding: Dust dominates over BC in absorption, snow albedo reduction, and radiative forcing in the Solu-Khumbu — dust forcing (488–525 W/m²) is 4–7× larger than BC forcing (75–120 W/m²) at Mera Glacier. This refutes single-agent 'soot' narratives; light-absorbing impurities are a mixed BC + dust signal.
elevational_pattern: BC and Fe (dust proxy) concentrations substantially elevated below 6,000 m a.s.l., driven by post-depositional processes and lower tropospheric loading
notes: Values used for Chapter 5 (light-absorbing impurities) of the Water-Cycle Atlas
Per WATER_CYCLE_SPEC.md §11: Ch 5 framing is 'light-absorbing impurities (BC + dust)', NOT BC-only 'soot apocalypse'
Dust proxy = Fe concentrations; paper does not speciate mineral dust further
Radiative forcing values are instantaneous and localized — not annual mean forcing
Sampling site: southern Himalayan slope; may differ from northern (Tibetan Plateau) slope dynamics
